summary: Automated valuation is the sector's oldest deployed AI, and it is now formally regulated: federal quality-control standards for AVMs took effect in 2025. Valuation, leasing automation, 3D capture, and property operations are where AI actually runs; the regulator record and the platforms' own model documentation are the sources.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 31.9% of firms in real estate and rental and leasing reported using AI in the last two weeks, up from 28.9% in the prior period. The survey first asked the question in September 2023, so the sector's measured adoption is recent but rising. The sources show AI concentrated in a few distinct functions rather than spread evenly across the industry.

Automated valuation is the oldest and most visible use. Zillow publishes Zestimates for 110+ million homes using a neural network based model that incorporates county and tax assessor records, MLS feeds, and hundreds of data points per property, with an estimated sales range to capture uncertainty. HouseCanary offers AI powered valuations, forecasts, and insights for over 136M U.S. properties, and its image recognition technology identifies room types and assesses home condition directly from photos. Opendoor's cash offer business, which has served over 309,390 homeowners, depends on pricing models that carry direct balance sheet exposure. These models are now federally regulated: the CFPB, FHFA, OCC, FDIC, NCUA, and the Federal Reserve Board adopted a final rule under the Dodd-Frank Act requiring mortgage originators and secondary market issuers to adopt quality control standards for automated valuation models, including protections against data manipulation, conflict of interest safeguards, and random sample testing.

Leasing and property operations are the other major deployment area. Prophia uses AI to extract key lease terms from commercial documents and combines it with expert validation to produce structured lease data that owners and operators can use for risk and decision making. EliseAI runs agentic conversational AI that schedules tours, answers prospect questions, follows up on leads, and handles maintenance requests around the clock. Building Engines, a JLL company, markets Prism as an AI powered platform that delivers instant answers, recommendations, and automation to help commercial property teams cut costs and grow net operating income. Matterport's 3D cameras and virtual tour software digitize buildings and integrate with Procore and Autodesk, positioning spatial data as the layer under virtual touring and property intelligence.

On the brokerage side, Compass applies AI to listing attributes, location, and prior search activity to surface relevant homes to buyers, and its Concierge program covers home improvement costs to help sellers close faster. JLL states it has invested more in AI technology than any other real estate company. The National Association of Realtors runs REACH through Second Century Ventures, which it describes as the most active venture fund in the global real estate technology space, and CRETI, the Center for Real Estate Technology and Innovation, tracks proptech capital as a research organization, though its published page carries a disclaimer that it does not invest or advise.

The regulatory posture is clearest around valuation. The interagency AVM rule is the first binding federal framework for the sector's core AI, and the CFPB's rule page frames it as consumer protection for collateral worth determinations on principal dwellings. For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the sources suggest the highest confidence uses are document extraction, conversational leasing automation, and 3D capture, while valuation models carry both the longest production history and the most explicit compliance obligations. Where the sources are silent on ROI figures, they are silent, and the vendor claims about cost reduction and productivity should be read as marketing rather than measured results.

https://creti.org/.brief: CRETI, the Center for Real Estate Technology & Innovation, is a research and education organization that focuses on the health and wellness of real-estate technology and related sectors. The site’s disclaimer states that the information it offers is for general information and entertainment purposes only, and that it is provided in good faith without any warranty of accuracy, validity, reliability, or completeness. CRETI explicitly says it does not invest in or advise on the investment of funds or technology companies. The organization’s stated purpose is to educate and research rather than to provide investment services.

https://prophia.com/.brief: Prophia turns lease documents into verified intelligence that uncovers risk, protects capital, and powers AI. It offers “AI-powered lease abstraction” that pulls key lease terms and then applies expert validation to ensure accuracy, producing clean, structured data that teams can use. The platform’s Prophia Essentials helps owners and operators manage tenants and investments by structuring, visualizing, and tracking every lease detail. The company claims this streamlines operations, mitigates risk, and improves decision-making with trusted portfolio data.

https://www.jll.com/.brief: JLL offers commercial real estate services and property investment strategies for owners, tenants, and investors worldwide. The company says it uses an innovative, intelligent, and optimistic approach to tackle complex challenges and shape a better future for real estate. JLL claims it has invested more in AI technology than any other real estate firm, and that this investment is unlocking the potential of buildings and people. Its website lists solutions such as space leasing, portfolio management, private investor services, hybrid workspaces, green building leasing, and AI-driven commercial real estate tools.

https://www.boma.org/.brief: BOMA/BOMI is a trade association that supports commercial real estate professionals by offering resources, legislative advocacy, and professional credentials. It partners with BOMA International and the Building Owners and Managers Institute to help members grow their careers and companies. Membership gives access to exclusive discounts on building supplies, office supplies, shipping, and merchant services. The organization also connects members with experts and provides tools to help them lead the industry.

https://matterport.com/.brief: Matterport’s platform lets users “Capture, share, and collaborate in immersive 3D” by digitizing buildings and automatically creating 3D tours, 4K photos, and schematic floor plans. It offers 3D insights that help centralize portfolio decisions, speed workplace planning, and reduce risk. The system integrates with Procore and Autodesk to cut time, lower site visits, and improve communication across a job. Users can manage operations from anywhere using real-time AWS data to lower costs, boost productivity, and raise ROI, while buyers and sellers gain confidence from immersive tours, floor plans, and high-quality photos.

https://www.compass.com/.brief: Compass says it uses a combination of listing attributes, location, prior search activity, and listing views to surface homes that may be relevant to users. It claims its concierge service covers home-improvement costs until closing, stating that the cost is “zero due until closing.” Compass notes that the data it displays comes from the Willamette Valley Multiple Listing Service, which it does not guarantee for accuracy and is provided “AS IS” with all faults. The company also states it does not discriminate against voucher holders, is an E-Verify employer, and does not offer financial or legal advice.

https://www.eliseai.com/.brief: EliseAI says it is an AI platform that aims to transform property management and healthcare by automating communications and boosting operational efficiency. It uses agentic conversational AI to handle messages, calls, and tasks automatically, integrating with existing systems to provide fast, personalized responses around the clock. The platform can schedule tours, answer complex questions, follow up with prospects, and manage maintenance or scheduling requests without human intervention. According to the company, its AI-driven automation streamlines workflows, cuts costs, and frees staff for higher-impact work.

https://www.nar.realtor/.brief: The National Association of REALTORS® is an American trade association that covers all aspects of residential and commercial real estate. It offers a range of resources for both new agents and experienced brokers, including information on home buying and selling, commercial and international markets, member services, and technology. The association provides training through its institutes, societies, and councils, and keeps members updated with daily news, events, and policy updates. NAR also manages its logo and trademark rules, and operates the REALTORS® Political Action Committee to support pro-REALTOR® candidates. Members can access designations and certifications to enhance their skills and earnings.

https://www.opendoor.com/.brief: Opendoor presents itself as a way to sell a home without listing, showings, or months of stress, letting sellers close on their own timeline and request a free offer. The page states that Opendoor has served more than 309,387 homeowners. Customer testimonials on the page describe the process as quick and painless, with one saying the offer came in near an appraisal and another calling the price fair. It also mentions a “Cash Now, More Later” option that combines a cash offer with proceeds from a market transaction.

https://www.housecanary.com/.brief: HouseCanary reports AI-powered valuations, forecasts, and insights for over 136 million U.S. properties. The platform curates and normalizes data from thousands of sources, using both AI-driven and manual quality-control systems to ensure accuracy, and employs image-recognition technology to identify property details from photos. HouseCanary says it delivers actionable insights in seconds, helping real-estate investors, agents, and loan officers make confident decisions and stay competitive. It also markets itself as the most trusted and reliable AI-powered data and analytics platform for residential real estate and a 50-state brokerage, claiming its difference lies in its data.

https://www.nar.realtor/reach.brief: REACH is a technology scale-up program created by Second Century Ventures, described on the page as a “unique technology scale-up program.” It offers a wide range of resources for both new agents and experienced brokers, covering home buying and selling, commercial and international markets, member information, and technology tools. The program encourages users to use data and the latest trends and statistics to improve their business. NAR also provides training options, daily news, events, and policy updates for REALTORS®, and reminds members that only they may use the REALTOR® name and logo.

https://www.zillow.com/z/zestimate/.brief: Zillow’s Zestimate is a free estimate of a home’s market value that blends public records, MLS data and user-submitted details. Zillow publishes Zestimates for more than 110 million homes and refreshes them several times a week, using a neural-network model that pulls county and tax assessor records and MLS feeds. The model also offers an estimated sales range to show the possible price span and updates when a home goes on the market or new data arrives. Over nearly 20 years, Zillow has refined the Zestimate by adding expanded historical data and seasonal trend adjustments to improve accuracy while keeping broad coverage.

https://www.consumerfinance.gov/rules-po.brief: The CFPB, OCC, FRB, FDIC, NCUA, and FHFA adopted a final rule that requires mortgage originators and secondary-market issuers to use automated valuation models (AVMs) that meet quality-control standards set by the Dodd-Frank Act. Under the rule, institutions involved in certain credit decisions or securitization must implement policies, practices, procedures, and control systems to ensure AVMs produce reliable estimates, guard against data manipulation, avoid conflicts of interest, and conduct random sample testing and reviews. The rule also mandates compliance with applicable regulations.

https://www.fhfa.gov/regulation/federal-.brief: The OCC, Board, FDIC, NCUA, CFPB, and FHFA collectively adopted a final rule that implements the quality control standards required by the Dodd-Frank Act for automated valuation models (AVMs). The rule applies to mortgage originators and secondary-market issuers who use AVMs to determine the collateral value of a consumer’s principal dwelling. Under the rule, institutions that make certain credit decisions or securitization determinations must establish policies, practices, procedures, and control systems so that AVMs meet “quality control standards” that ensure a high level of confidence in the estimates, guard against data manipulation, and avoid conflicts of interest.
